steps.prompt:
Create a NEW cohesive Suzhou Chinese market STREET environment asset for a walkable 2D game, based closely on the three provided reference images' architecture, material detail, composition and warm painterly anime style. This is one real connected neighborhood street, not a collection of freestanding kiosks, NOT two canal islands, NOT a mobile city builder. Output 1536x1024 transparent PNG.
CAMERA: consistent elevated orthographic three-quarter view, looking north along the street, parallel projection. Warm daylight. Architectural scale like the references with full small two-storey timber-and-white-plaster shophouses, connected tiled roofs, adjoining upper story lattice balconies, lanterns and laundry.
EXACT GROUND PLAN: A continuous pale stone pedestrian street runs vertically from the top edge to bottom edge centered at x=850. Its CLEAR WALKABLE GROUND stays at least 230 pixels wide at EVERY y: the strip x=735 to x=965 from y=0 to y=1024 must remain unblocked paving. This is a lively narrow neighborhood lane wide enough for two characters to pass, not a plaza. Connected building rows flank the street. LEFT row footprint x=260..700: two adjoining long shops, breakfast upper half and pastries lower half, shop fronts face the center street to the right. RIGHT row footprint x=1000..1480: three adjoining shops, fans upper third, produce middle third, noodle restaurant lower third, shop fronts face the center street to the left. Never place roofs, signs, stalls or baskets inside x735..965 walking lane. Roofs and counters face inward to enclose the street, shared side walls and connected eaves make each row one coherent town block. Ground paving also connects around the southern end of both rows and north end. Buildings stop 100 pixels before bottom edge to allow a cross street. Complete roofs and walls within the image, no chopped objects.
CANAL: ONLY ONE canal runs OUTSIDE the district along the LEFT edge x=0..170. Canal water is TRUE ALPHA TRANSPARENT so the game draws water underneath. A continuous detailed stone quay wall at x=175..210 divides water from a modest outer waterside walkway x210..260. Make one open bridge landing into the market at left edge around y200, with a 115px-wide unobstructed side passage continuing to the central street BETWEEN the two left shop portions (this access passage may split their ground floor, but a timber second-floor gallery can join the building row behind the passage). NO water, canals, bridges or moats down the central street or between other shops.
Clear Chinese shop signs: 包子 at upper left, 糕点 lower left, 扇子 upper right, 水果 and 蔬菜 middle right, 面 and 小吃 lower right. Small outward fabric awnings, steamers and bowls, stools tucked at walls, red lanterns hung under eaves, wall-rooted vines, baskets tucked at counters. More structural architecture and lived-in detail than excessive flowers. Keep roofs narrower than first floors so they don't hide the street. Border of natural complete stone quays on west, small rooted planting and complete foundation stones elsewhere. True transparency outside complete natural perimeter; no glow, vignette, blurred fade or checkerboard pixels.
NO people, animals, UI, text bubbles, portrait panels or map labels. We add moving characters separately. Do not reproduce UI from reference. The entire 230px central paved route MUST stay clear and visible from top to bottom; it is the defining composition. Return a complete coherent walkable town street that feels like the references, not separately spaced huts.

Finish this exact market STREET composition as a clean game asset. Preserve the coherent adjoining shophouse rows, architectural design, the Chinese signs, and the generous continuous central walking lane. Do not return to separate kiosks or add an interior canal. Keep this view and daylight.
Necessary cleanup:
1. Remove ALL water pixels, lily pads, floating shadows and ALL hanging willow branches along the far LEFT. They must become TRUE ALPHA TRANSPARENCY. Keep the entire stone quay wall and the waterside pedestrian lane. No loose floating leaves.
2. Remove the small cropped bridge on the left edge around y250, including every deck, railing and post over the canal. Leave a clean opening/stone landing in the bank for a separate bridge rendered by the game. The landing is an open section in the wall, not a bridge span.
3. Remove the two foreground partial roof fragments at the bottom edge entirely. Continue the open cross lane and end it in a clean complete natural stone pavement edge.
4. Zoom the entire district out by about 10% to fit all buildings FULLY within the canvas, and complete the presently cut-off top roof lines and far right roof tips. Leave a little transparent margin around complete architectural silhouettes. No roofs, walls or foliage cut by any canvas edge.
5. Retain the generous continuous middle walking lane AT LEAST 220px clear width from the north opening to the south opening, and the west-side waterfront lane at least 85px clear width. Do not add plants on these routes. Keep the central paving straight and parallel-edged, no forced perspective shrinking toward the top.
6. Outside the district's complete buildings/pavement edges and in canal areas there must be true alpha transparency, NO water, background color, vignette, blurred fade or glow. Natural solid perimeter all around, with clearly open north and south lane exits. No boundary wall blocking the center lane at north or south.
1536x1024 transparent PNG. NO characters, no UI. Preserve legible 包子, 糕点, 扇子, 水果, 蔬菜, 面, 小吃. This is a precise production cleanup, not a redesign.

Revise this Suzhou market asset. The user LIKES this architectural style and density, but the single long straight street is too rigid. Make its layout organic with L-SHAPED CONNECTED SHOP BLOCKS, crossing alleys, different rows and columns of shops, and small varied courtyards. Keep a coherent neighborhood of adjoining substantial two-storey shophouses, not isolated kiosks or equally spaced huts. Keep the warm hand-painted anime finish, complete roofs, white plaster, lattice balconies, readable Chinese shop signs, lanterns and tucked-in everyday shop goods.
LAYOUT REVISION: Keep five recognizable shopfronts: breakfast 包子, pastries 糕点, fans 扇子, produce 水果/蔬菜, noodles 面/小吃. Break the existing two perfectly straight parallel rows into three staggered L-shaped connected building blocks. The breakfast block in the northwest has a short perpendicular rear return making an L. The fan/produce block in the northeast has adjoining shopfronts turning a corner so one faces west and one faces south. The pastries/noodles toward the south form a staggered lower row with a small open corner court. Shops are differently oriented along north-south and east-west lanes. At least two frontages should face south along a cross alley instead of all facing the central street. Every shop belongs to a proper connected building frontage with architectural depth.
WALKABILITY IS ESSENTIAL: The main central route bends gently through the market and stays 180-220 pixels clear. Make TWO clear paved cross alleys, each 110-140 pixels clear, one connecting the western quay landing across the upper-middle of the market, another connecting the center to the east side in the lower-middle. Paths connect into a loop around blocks, with visible intersections. No narrow residual gaps, no roof or plants covering the clear routes. Avoid a big empty plaza: small irregular junctions, intimate street feeling like the existing art. Whole footprint still 1536x1024. Fit all five shopfronts with these useful lanes.
EDGES MUST BE COMPLETE AND STANDALONE: Entire buildings and all roof tips fully inside canvas with transparent margin. Continuous complete stone canal quay only along the western outside edge, with one open bridge landing but ABSOLUTELY NO BRIDGE ART. No canal inside the market. ALL background and ALL water areas are TRUE ALPHA TRANSPARENT; game draws water. No tree branches unless entire trunk and roots are included; prefer wall-rooted vines and small complete pots, NO TREES. No boats. No cropped foreground roofs or leaves. No haze, glows, blurred fade, water pixels, checkerboard, or rectangular backdrop. Natural clean fully drawn perimeter with open pedestrian exits where lanes meet it. Keep canvas margins all sides. No characters, UI, portraits, labels or people. High quality coherent organic Suzhou street district with L blocks and clearly usable alleys.

Precise walkability adjustment to this approved organic Suzhou market district, preserve its L-shaped architecture, layout, all five shops, signs, transparent edges and overall composition. Change only these two pinched passages:
A) NORTH EXIT: The opening at top center around x760..830 y120 is too thin. Widen it to a CLEAR 160-pixel stone passage centered x800. Move the upper-left rear return wall/roof edge left to x715 and the upper-right return wall/roof edge right to x885 in that small north entry area. Continue the widened pavement down into the existing bending center lane. Keep the full rooftops within canvas, fully drawn.
B) WEST CROSS ALLEY: The passage between the breakfast block and lower-left pastry block is too thin. Move ONLY the rear/top edge of the lower-left pastry block DOWN about 85 pixels, shortening its building depth while retaining its storefront, two storeys, L-shaped return and its current bottom edge near y925. The stone cross alley from the west quay landing near x100 y435 to the main intersection near x850 y460 should now have at least 120 pixels of visible clear depth, especially across x300..750. Remove pots intruding into this clear crossing and tuck them at the walls. Keep its ground entry level and walkable.
Do not enlarge overall canvas footprint or add empty plazas. Retain all other current buildings, routes, distinctive turns and side alleys exactly. No new canal, bridge, tree, people, background, water or loose leaves. Clean complete natural district edges and true alpha transparent surroundings, 1536x1024. Preserve all current Chinese signs.

processing: Copied losslessly; browser draws original alpha over shared town water. Collision traced to the final artwork.
